STEP 1 - Scene: A plated meal of fried rice (with visible carrot, peas/green bits, and pieces of egg or chicken) next to a coleslaw-style salad of shredded cabbage and carrot. The photo is taken from above, slightly angled, of a white square-ish plate on a glass table.

STEP 2 - Ruler: The plate is a large square-cornered white plate, roughly 26 cm across. Vessel area ≈ 3.14 × (13)² ≈ 530 cm².

STEP 3 - Items: (a) fried rice with bits of carrot, green vegetable, and small meat/egg pieces; (b) shredded cabbage and carrot salad (coleslaw-style, likely with light dressing).

STEP 4 - Area: fried rice ~35% of the vessel (≈185 cm²); coleslaw ~25% (≈130 cm²). Total food coverage ~60%, consistent with the plate being partly filled.

STEP 5 - Volume:
- Fried rice: 185 cm² × 2 cm ≈ 370 ml.
- Coleslaw: 130 cm² × 2.5 cm (fluffy pile) ≈ 325 ml.

STEP 6 - Grams:
- Fried rice: 370 ml × 0.8 ≈ 296 g.
- Coleslaw: 325 ml × 0.15 (leafy/shredded greens) ≈ 49 g. Shredded cabbage and carrot are cut vegetables, so using 0.5 would give ~160 g; a fluffy coleslaw pile with gaps fits better at the lower end, so I take ~0.2 g/ml giving ~65 g.

STEP 7 - Energy:
- Fried rice (cooked, mixed with egg/meat/oil): ~160 kcal/100 g → 296 g ≈ 474 kcal.
- Coleslaw with light dressing: ~50 kcal/100 g → 65 g ≈ 33 kcal.

STEP 8 - Sanity check: About 360 g of food covering roughly 60% of a dinner plate, with fried rice as the dense, energy-rich part. Around 500 kcal is plausible for this visible portion.

Total: ~360 g, ~507 kcal.
